command:# Reports live under temporary-docs/gnomish/<task>/: the task branch's name without its
# gnomish/ prefix (the factory's own sanitized taskId), 'local' off a task branch.
branch=$(git branch --show-current)
case "$branch" in gnomish/*) task=${branch#gnomish/} ;; *) task=local ;; esac
dir=temporary-docs/gnomish/$task
if [ ! -f $dir/change.md ]; then
  echo "no change record at $dir/change.md - write it before finishing the round"
  exit 1
fi

command:# Reports live under temporary-docs/gnomish/<task>/: the task branch's name without its
# gnomish/ prefix (the factory's own sanitized taskId), 'local' off a task branch.
branch=$(git branch --show-current)
case "$branch" in gnomish/*) task=${branch#gnomish/} ;; *) task=local ;; esac
dir=temporary-docs/gnomish/$task
report=$dir/change.md
change=$(sed -n 's/^Change:[[:space:]]*//p' "$report" | head -1)
if [ -z "$change" ]; then
  echo "the report has no 'Change: <name>' line - name the change the task asked about"
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$change" = "archive" ] || [ ! -d "openspec/changes/$change" ]; then
  echo "the report names change '$change', but openspec/changes/$change is not an active change directory"
  exit 1
fi
# A length check deliberately does NOT live here. The report's size budget is
# in the instructions, where it shapes the writing for free; as a check it
# would fail a correct, usable verdict and buy a whole second round - a new
# analysis from scratch - to reformat prose. That costs more than every
# verbose report it could ever prevent, and on a second miss it escalates to
# a human over formatting. A check earns its round only when its failure
# means the output is unusable or unsafe, which is what the other three are.
verdict=$(sed -n 's/^Verdict:[[:space:]]*//p' "$report" | head -1)
if [ "$verdict" != "no-blocking-dependencies" ]; then
  echo "the report's verdict is '$verdict'; the only verdict that finishes this stage is 'no-blocking-dependencies'."
  echo "If the change IS blocked, do not finish the round: write the dependency chain to the path in \$GNOMISH_DECISION_FILE as {\"question\": \"...\", \"options\": [\"...\"]} and end your turn - the factory posts it to the tracker and parks the task for a human."
  exit 1
fi

command:# Reports live under temporary-docs/gnomish/<task>/: the task branch's name without its
# gnomish/ prefix (the factory's own sanitized taskId), 'local' off a task branch.
branch=$(git branch --show-current)
case "$branch" in gnomish/*) task=${branch#gnomish/} ;; *) task=local ;; esac
dir=temporary-docs/gnomish/$task
report=$dir/change.md
dirty=$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | sed 's/^...//' | grep -v "^$report$" || true)
if [ -n "$dirty" ]; then
  echo "this stage writes only $report, but the working copy also carries:"
  echo "$dirty"
  echo "if you made these edits, undo each of them yourself and nothing else."
  echo "if you did not: an in-place run measures the operator's own clone, so these are someone else's work in progress. Leave every one of them exactly as it is - do not stash, restore, checkout or clean anything - write no report, and escalate through \$GNOMISH_DECISION_FILE naming the paths."
  exit 1
fi
# Committed strays, measured from the merge base with origin/main - not from
# origin/main itself: the factory keeps that ref current, and a plain diff
# against it would list everything that landed since the branch was cut.
# Skipped off a task branch (an in-place run has no branch of its own to
# measure) and when origin/main is not at hand. `.gnomish-task/` is the
# factory's own bookkeeping, never the gnome's work.
branch=$(git branch --show-current)
case "$branch" in
  gnomish/*)
    if base=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD 2>/dev/null); then
      committed=$(git diff --name-only "$base" HEAD | grep -v "^$report$" | grep -v "^\.gnomish-task/" || true)
      if [ -n "$committed" ]; then
        echo "the branch carries committed changes this stage had no business making:"
        echo "$committed"
        exit 1
      fi
    fi
    ;;
esac
